Agreement on scoped workloads, access gating (VPC + SFTP samples), mid-point perf review and exec readout. Some security clarifications needed around KMS and data retention.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Victor (Redwood SE), Sophie (Nimbus Head of ML), Carlos (Eng Manager), Diane (Head of Security), Alex (Product), Rina (Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary: short POC kickoff, agreed on critical path items.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick round robin, if you can say your role and main success metric for this POC.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Sophie, Head of ML at Nimbus. We're looking to validate whether Redwood can meet our 95th percentile latency under 400ms for triage generation and that cost per 1k tokens is below our SaaS threshold.
00:27 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Carlos here, we care about integration complexity and how much engineering effort to go live.
00:36 Speaker 4 (Diane): Diane, security. Need clarity on KMS, audit logs, and data residency obligations for PHI-ish metadata.
00:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, that's helpful. Victor on the SE side will walk through the proposed milestones. Victor?
00:56 Speaker 5 (Victor): Thanks. I'll share my screen — but for the transcript I'll just run through the milestones. We propose a 3-week POC: week 0 kickoff & access, week 1 baseline benchmarks and feature gating, week 2 tuning, mid-point review at end of week 1, exec readout in week 3. Kickoff tasks: access to a VPC endpoint or token for hosted route, sample request traces, and a target set of prompts.
01:29 Speaker 2 (Sophie): On traces — we can share anonymized request logs, about 7 days. Hope that's enough. Also our 95th perc includes cold starts if possible.
01:42 Speaker 5 (Victor): That's perfect, the traces help with batching and seq length distribution. Cold start testing we can simulate but want to understand your traffic pattern — lots of short chats or longer clinical summaries?
01:58 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Mostly short to mid-length, average 120 tokens, 95th at ~520 tokens on some case summaries.
02:10 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Question — should we go Dedicated or Hosted for the POC? We are sensitive to data but want speed to results.
02:20 Speaker 5 (Victor): For initial perf benchmarks we recommend hosted with a VPC peering or private endpoint — it's fastest to iterate. Dedicated reserved capacity is an option if you want predictable throughput later, but it adds procurement lead time.
02:37 Speaker 4 (Diane): From security perspective, we prefer Private deployment, but for the POC we can accept a VPC private endpoint if we get KMS integration and audit logs.
02:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We'll include KMS flow and audit log export in the security pack. Diane, can you outline what compliance docs you expect during the POC?
03:05 Speaker 4 (Diane): SOC2 type II evidence, encryption at rest and in transit, RBAC controls, SAML SSO, and data retention policy. Also want to understand how Redwood handles KV cache for prompts — we can't keep PHI in cache unless it's encrypted.
03:22 Speaker 5 (Victor): Quick note — our KV cache can be configured to not persist or to encrypt with customer KMS. We'll add config examples to the playbook. (murmur) 
03:35 Speaker 6 (Alex): Product question: what's the gate for success internally? Is it purely perf+cost or also qualitative eval?
03:42 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Both. Primary is perf/cost; secondary is hallucination rate under our eval set — we have a list of 120 prompts to run. If hallucination > 8% we won't move forward.
03:55 Speaker 5 (Victor): Good — we'll run the eval harness and include rouge/precision-like metrics plus a human-in-the-loop error sample. We'll also run a benchmark against your longest prompt set.
04:12 Speaker 7 (Rina): On sample data movement: we prefer to SFTP anonymized test payloads versus opening a public bucket. Is that supported?
04:20 Speaker 5 (Victor): Yes SFTP or private VPC peering both supported. We'll document steps.
04:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): I'm going to read out the milestone dates we tentatively discussed. Kickoff today (2026-02-20), access completed by 2026-02-24, baseline benchmarks by 2026-02-28, mid-point review 2026-03-01, tuning 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-12, exec readout 2026-03-19. Thoughts?
04:56 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Those look fine, but procurement might push on dedicated billing if we pick reserved capacity.
05:04 Speaker 5 (Victor): We can run the POC on hosted to avoid procurement friction. If you want predictable latency we can demonstrate Dedicated in a follow-up.
05:14 Speaker 4 (Diane): One more security ask: we need to confirm data deletion timelines after POC and whether any logs containing tokens are retained.
05:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll include a data retention spec — Redwood's default is 30 days for logs, but for POCs we can offer shorter retention or manual purge on request. We'll confirm dates in writing.
05:37 Speaker 2 (Sophie): On benchmarks, how will you measure cost? Token-based, GPU-hours, or both?
05:44 Speaker 5 (Victor): We'll provide both. Cost per 1k tokens and cost per 1k requests with breakdown for compute, batch efficiency, and KV-cache hit rate. We'll include a sample spreadsheet link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/nimbus-poc-template (placeholder).
06:02 Speaker 6 (Alex): Will you simulate production concurrency patterns or just single-stream latency?
06:09 Speaker 5 (Victor): Both. We'll run single-stream p95 latency and also concurrent throughput tests that emulate your trace concurrency. That helps us recommend batching and slot sizes.
06:20 Speaker 7 (Rina): Who owns the test harness? Do we run scripts or do you?
06:25 Speaker 5 (Victor): We'll provide a harness and scripts. For hosted testing you'll run the harness from your environment against the endpoint. We can also run remote runs if you authorize Redwood engineers.
06:38 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Ok that helps. Procurement will need an estimate of peak cost for a 1 month pilot — even rough numbers are useful.
06:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll provide an estimated cost model based on your token distributions. I'll get that to you with the access playbook.
06:55 Speaker 2 (Sophie): On hallucination metrics — can you support reranker/eval flow? We may want a reranking pass to improve precision.
07:03 Speaker 5 (Victor): Yes we support reranking and can include that in the POC scope as an optional gate. We'll baseline without rerank first, then try rerank to show delta.
07:14 Speaker 4 (Diane): We also need to confirm SAML SSO for console access for our reviewers; not just API keys.
07:21 Speaker 1 (Maya): SAML is supported. We'll include a quickstart SSO doc in the pack.
07:30 Speaker 2 (Sophie): One slight concern — you mentioned quantization recommendations previously; will that affect model fidelity for clinical texts?
07:39 Speaker 5 (Victor): We'll include model and quantization matrix. For clinical text we usually recommend FP16 or 8-bit float quant with eval checks; we'll capture quality regressions in the eval harness.
07:55 Speaker 6 (Alex): Is there an NDA addendum for PHI handling during the POC?
08:01 Speaker 1 (Maya): We can sign a short POC addendum; legal will prepare.
08:07 Speaker 4 (Diane): Please route to our legal contact — Diane.Rowe@nimbushealth.example (note: placeholder).
08:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. Ok, quick recap of next steps then I'll close.
08:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Action items: I'll send access playbook, Victor will send benchmark harness and template, Sophie to share traces, Diane to confirm security contact and requirements. We'll tentatively plan the mid-point review for 2026-03-01 and exec readout 2026-03-19.
08:34 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
08:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks, we'll follow up via email and I'll cc everyone with the checklist. Bye.
08:44 Meeting end.
notes: Transcript contains occasional recognition errors (V P C sometimes transcribed as V P C, KV cache as K V cash). References to internal links are placeholders. Participants agreed on a 3-week POC with explicit gates: access, baseline, mid-point, exec readout.
